title: The interim look after development (dev-01 to dev-05; hp-01 is counted in stage 1 and its table is lm-hp-01, RL-167 §3), as RL-166 to RL-167 rule it. Stage 1, which opens no energy file, gives the inclusion verdicts, the roster, the rates, the start-reading medians and the onset model. Stage 2 gives the segment fit (count-only base, start-reading ramp and onset step) on the GPU rail and DC-in, its leave-one-day-out errors, the prefix bias and step 3's drift statistic. Freeze 2 follows. DRAFT: pins are on a draft basis until the cold reviews close.

when.describe_blocks_rule: hp-01 is counted in stage 1 only: its inclusion verdicts and the hp01_below_9 tripwire. Stage 2 opens no hp-01 energy, and the High Power table is look lm-hp-01, with its own manifest, committed before any hp-01 energy or in-turn clock is opened (RL-167 §3). A reserve leg serving development enters if it is desk-final when stage 1 runs; the look does not wait for one (RL-166 Q13). If fewer than 9 of hp-01's included type-A legs are counted, the research lead is told before stage 2 (RL-157 §4; RL-166 Q8; RL-167 §2 row 21).
before: the W1 receipt is signed, for the drift tripwire (RL-151 §1.3 item 2)

holds.rule: If true in stage 1's committed output, the lead holds stage 2 until the research lead clears it. The fit does not refuse on it (RL-166c §2 row 7; RL-166b P-4).
If true in stage 1's committed output, the lead holds stage 2 until the research lead clears it. The fit does not refuse on it (RL-166c §2 row 7; RL-167 R-20).
If any of Q8's five tripwires fired in stage 1's committed output, stage 1 goes to the research lead and the lead holds stage 2 until it is cleared (RL-166 Q8).

stages.tripwire_action: Any tripwire sends stage 1's output to the research lead before stage 2. So does P-4's count above zero when the onset model is not_estimable. Otherwise stage 2 runs on the lead's record.

reads.day_rule: A leg's calendar day is the local date of its span's t0 (RL-155a §1.2). A block's pilot and remainder on one date are one day (RL-155 §2 notes). A reserve leg keeps its own day (RL-166 Q13). The day is the unit of every leave-one-out error (RL-149 §2.3).

heat_term.segments: Per leg: the prefill (turn start stamp to the first token), and each full 256-token decode block in step 3's convention (block 0 = [t(tok 0), t(tok 255)], block k >= 1 = [t(tok 256k-1), t(tok 256k+255)]). A leg's prefix is a shorter leg (RL-149 §2.2).
heat_term.count_clock: The prefill ends at T_p = P / r_p; decode token m falls at T_p + m / r_d. A segment covers [u, v] on this clock, with d = v - u and midpoint m = (u + v) / 2.
heat_term.start_readings: z1 start Tf08, z2 start fan rpm, z3 start TV0h less the span's soak reference. Each taken under RL-149 §1.3's start rule (the last journal reading at or before the turn start, at most 2 s before it, with a fresh pm stamp), and centred on its median over included development legs. The medians are stage-1 constants. Active readings only (RL-166b B-2): stage 1 decides, on energy-fit legs, that a reading is active when, for every fit day D, at least 6 energy-fit legs off day D have |z| above its tolerance (0.25 degC for Tf08 and for TV0h excess, 25 rpm for the fan). An inactive reading's kappa column and onset predictor are dropped in the main fit, every fold and the marked-spans print; stage 1 prints active_readings with the three counts, and the lead tells the research lead of any inactive reading. Stage 2 does not wait. TV0h excess keeps its median centre (RL-166b §2.3).
heat_term.form: Heat term of a segment [u, v]: d * m * (k_tf08 z1 + k_fan z2 + k_tv0h z3) + delta * w~, where w~ is the expected hot seconds under the onset model (RL-166b B-1): w~ = sigma * [G((v - l)/sigma) - G((u - l)/sigma)], G(x) = x Phi(x) + phi(x), Phi(x) = erfc(-x/sqrt 2)/2, phi(x) = exp(-x^2/2)/sqrt(2 pi); l is the onset model's linear predictor, not clipped; sigma is that onset fit's ML sigma (sigma_s). The main fit uses the main onset fit and a fold its own. A start_out_of_state leg takes w~ = d. If sigma is under 1e-6 s, w~ is the plain overlap with [tau_hat, inf). For a turn: H = 1/2 T^2 (k . z) + delta * sigma * [G((T - l)/sigma) - G(-l/sigma)], T the turn's count-derived load seconds. tau_hat = max(0, l), the count-only cut, the hot stretch (R-4) and R-13's error do not change; l is formed in stage 2 from stage 1's coefficients and readings. No sign is assumed for any of the four. RL-166's sentence that H is exactly 0 before the predicted onset is withdrawn (RL-166b Amends).
heat_term.response: The segment's energy on the channel (energy.channels).
heat_term.base: A count-only base, fitted jointly and never exported as H: prefill p1 P + p2 P^2; decode block a0 n + a1 n c + a2 n P, with n = edge_hi - edge_lo (255 for block 0, 256 for k >= 1, a prefix tail's own count; RL-166a R-2) and c = P + (edge_lo + 1 + edge_hi) / 2, the context tokens at the block's midpoint (RL-166a R-3).
heat_term.estimation: Ordinary least squares per channel on the columns p1, p2, a0, a1, a2, k_tf08, k_fan, k_tv0h, delta (as the interface names them), less any column dropped by B-2 or by an onset model that is not estimable. The solve (RL-166b B-6): each design column is divided by its RMS over rows; the solve is SVD or QR on that matrix (numpy.linalg.lstsq is enough) and the coefficients are scaled back; rank-deficient means the smallest singular value is under 1e-10 of the largest; the normal matrix is never formed in raw units. Parameter covariance clustered by leg, CR1 (R-10). The onset's scatter is in the delta column; the onset coefficients' own uncertainty is not propagated (RL-166b Amends). Freeze 2 takes the fit on all included development legs; the with/without-marked-spans fit is a print and never replaces it.
heat_term.missing_start_reading: A leg with a missing or stale start reading is not in the fit and is counted (RL-166 Q1).
heat_term.out_of_state_start: A leg whose start reading is out of state takes tau_hat = 0 (RL-166 Q1).
heat_term.onset_not_estimable: If the onset model is not_estimable, the delta column is dropped and the print says so (RL-166 Q1). A LODO fold whose own onset fit fails RL-166b B-4 drops delta in that fold only.
heat_term.outside_calibrated_range: The calibrated range of each start reading (min and max over included development legs) is a stage-1 constant frozen in freeze 2; a later reading outside it sets heat_extrapolated (RL-149 §2.7).

rates.r_p: sum of P over sum of (first_token_s - turn_start_s), over included development legs (RL-166a R-1)
rates.r_d: sum of (N - 1) over sum of (last_token_s - first_token_s), over included development legs (RL-166a R-1)
rates.per_cell: per-cell rates print beside them and are used nowhere

onset.response: Seconds from the turn's start stamp to the first off-state reading in (turn start, last token]: a journal reading with OS level above 0, whatever its stamp's age, or a journal reading or native powermetrics row whose state is present and is neither Nominal nor Unknown (RL-166a R-4; RL-167 §2 row 3). A state_unobserved gap is not one. Not from the first decode token: a 19.5k prefill can reach the cut.
onset.censoring: Right-censored at the last token; censored-normal maximum likelihood, hand-coded. tau_hat = max(0, the linear predictor). Legs that start out of state or hit state_unobserved are left out and counted.
onset.estimable_when: The main onset fit is estimable with at least 12 uncensored onsets on at least 3 calendar days, at least 4 uncensored onsets in each of at least two prompt-size cells (RL-166b B-3), and RL-166b B-5's convergence test passing; otherwise not_estimable, and the count-only cut stays at 116 s only if P-4's count is zero. A fold's onset fit needs at least 6 uncensored onsets on its training legs, at least 2 in each of at least two cells, and B-5; otherwise that fold drops delta (RL-166b B-4, amending RL-167 row 7). B-5, at the returned point whatever the optimiser: in Olsen's parameters (gamma = beta/sigma, eta = 1/sigma), with each predictor column and the responses and censoring times divided by their RMS over the fitted legs, all values finite and eta above 0; the negative Hessian positive definite with condition number at most 1e10; the Newton decrement g'(-H)^-1 g at most 1e-8. A central difference of the analytic gradient may stand in for an analytic Hessian. Stage 1 prints the uncensored count by cell. A censored share (n_censored over n_uncensored + n_censored) above 0.30 goes from the lead to the research lead; the reported error may then understate (RL-166b item 3.2).
onset.error: The RMS of predicted less observed over held-out uncensored legs, leave-one-day-out. Held-out censored legs with tau_hat under their censoring time are counted and printed.
onset.count_only_cut: tau_hat less twice the error (RL-149 §4 item 1)

validation.hot_stretch: A leg's full decode blocks whose first token is stamped at or after its first off-state reading as fit.onset.response defines it (RL-166a R-4). A leg with no such reading has none. tau_hat never sets it (RL-166a R-9).
validation.relative_error: For held-out day D: |sum predicted - sum measured| / sum measured over D's hot blocks, with the base, the heat term and the onset model all fitted without D. The rates and medians are not refitted per fold; they read no energy. 'Over the leg' is the same over all of a leg's segments.
validation.qualified_rule: The maximum over counted days, GPU rail, at or under 0.02. A day counts with at least three included legs that have a hot stretch. Fewer than three counted days prints not_evaluable, which is no.
validation.also_printed: each day's signed value; the pooled value; the RMS over held-out legs (the frozen holdout relative error of SD_j); and all of them again with the heat columns removed

prefix_bias.short: its prefix of 3,724, 3,151 or 2,981 decode tokens (ratios 1.10, 1.30, 1.374)
prefix_bias.residuals: leave-one-day-out, each divided by the SD of its own length over legs
prefix_bias.statistic: the mean of the day means; its 90 % t interval uses the same equal-day weights

step3.method: The adapter loads the committed module, rebinds LEGS and ORIGINAL_EIGHT to the roster and calls analyse and custody_check, once per prompt-size cell. It contains no arithmetic on energy. Any edit to the step 3 bytes needs a ruling. Custody mode: `python3 -I -B joulewise/cadence_looks/step3_roster.py --manifest M --stage1 S1 --stage1-sha256 H --custody ROOT --out STEP3.json`; the stage-2 CLI does not compute statistic (iii).
step3.tripwire_reads: the largest drift_fraction_linear over cells whose gamma is estimable; the 10k cell prints first, as the like-for-like value
step3.leg_failure: A leg on which analyse_leg raises is named with the exception's type, left out of that cell and counted. More than two in a cell: the cell prints not_run and comes to the research lead.

sensitivity: The fit with and without spans marked 'reference from an excluded leg' (RL-161 §4) or 'reference from a redo' (RL-158 Q2), in one print (RL-166 Q20). It never replaces the freeze-2 fit.
The fit and its errors with the heat columns removed (RL-166 Q3).
Prompt size enters through the count-only base, never as a cell effect (RL-166 Q1; RL-158 Q7).
reads_never: any slot, instruction or v4 label

stated_limits.text: yes means that on every counted day the held-out hot-stretch energy on the GPU rail was predicted within 2 %.

In simulation at the design's assumed spreads, a correct model gets yes 0.421 of the time (± 0.0025; about 4 times in 10; 0.001 to 0.693 over all twelve worlds in the committed evidence, with 0.421 in the default world) and a fit with no heat term 0.095 of the time (± 0.0015; about 1 time in 10.5). So no is the more likely word for a correct model. It is not evidence that the term is wrong, and no text may read it that way.
stated_limits.note: Figures from the RL-166b pass-rate re-run with B-1's column: Mythos 5.2 seat, Sat 14 Nov 2026 22:19:48 PST, 40,000 synthetic campaigns in the default world (two seeds of 20,000), 20,000 per other world; no measurement opened. Held at docs/process/cadence/looks/evidence/2026-11-14-mythos-passrate-rerun-REPORT.md (sha256 f1c6bc323d736bb13483a1783266d652f6eea2d347b93ed6e5a307ae614773aa). The correct-model rate lies inside RL-166b's 0.25 to 0.60, so nothing went to the research lead.

stated_limits.text: The pooled error does not discriminate: it is under 2 % with or without the heat term.

The start term is 3 % of its 439 s value on a 75 s turn and 12 % at 150 s. On turns under about 150 s, H is the onset step alone. Whether a warm start changes the energy of a short turn was not estimated.

Ĥ is a partial correction. In simulation it carries 0.84 to 0.96 of the heat effect over twelve simulated worlds, and 0.88 in the default one (0.79 before this change). The rest sits in the count-only base, which is not exported. That share cannot be measured on the campaign's own legs.
stated_limits.note: Verbatim from RL-166c §5. Figures from the RL-166b re-run, held at docs/process/cadence/looks/evidence/2026-11-14-mythos-passrate-rerun-REPORT.md (sha256 f1c6bc323d736bb13483a1783266d652f6eea2d347b93ed6e5a307ae614773aa), section 'Attenuation of delta'.

stated_limits.text: H is no longer exactly zero for a turn that ends before its predicted onset. A turn ending 20 s before it, at a scatter of 15 s, carries 0.6 expected hot seconds.
delta's clustered standard error overstates its spread (about 1.8 times in the planted world). The onset coefficients' own uncertainty is still not propagated.

Warm series turns are mostly outside the campaign's joint range of start readings (67 to 75 % in simulation), though inside each marginal range. A leverage flag beside heat_extrapolated is fixed for freeze 2.
1.10, 1.30 and 1.374 name ratios of decode tokens. The ratio of load seconds is smaller and prints by cell.
A pass of the 2 s clock-fit excess bound does not prove there is no hidden hole. Stage 1 prints the number of energy-fit legs with excess greater than 1 s and at most 2 s; this count decides nothing.

rules.text: It ran to its decode cap, or was cut by T_dead where the design says it should be.

Over the leg's interval (G0's start to the last stamped token): sidecar coverage at least 99 % and no gap over 2 s; powermetrics gaps at most max(1 s, 5 periods), U1's registered number (pilot_protocol_v4.md:451). Coverage and gap are the registered U1 evaluator's definitions (thermal.Coverage; thermal_desk.member_record's pm_gap), copied with a cite and an equality test because both are v4 strict paths. Delivered to stage 1 as the verdict file {"<span_id>/<leg_id>": {"sidecar_coverage": bool, "km003c_clean": bool}} (`python3 -I -B joulewise/cadence_looks/inclusion_34.py --manifest M ...`).

Header and trailer both present with a normal stop reason; inside the leg's interval, samples at least 99 % of the header's nominal rate (the count n of each sample line, summed, against sps x the interval) and no gap over 2 s between polls that carried samples (n > 0). Stamps and counts only: each sample line's rt and n are taken by pattern and the line dropped; no sample value is decoded (Sol cold seat N5). The span trailer's counts print in the inclusion table and decide nothing. Delivered to stage 1 as the verdict file {"<span_id>/<leg_id>": {"sidecar_coverage": bool, "km003c_clean": bool}} (`python3 -I -B joulewise/cadence_looks/inclusion_34.py --manifest M ...`).
It is not an attempt judged contaminated under the load-redo rule (above 0.5 core of outside load for 60 s), whether or not a redo replaced it.
The power mode is the block's.

inclusion.interval: G0's start to the last stamped token, for rules 3 and 4

decisions.statistic: the largest step-3 drift_fraction_linear over prompt-size cells whose gamma is estimable (GPU rail)
decisions.rule: Above the threshold: the S row comes back to the research lead before the W1 receipt is signed. Otherwise nothing happens. Condition (RL-166 Q11): the cold seat confirms from the step 4 note that 8 % is a simulated cell with the rows at or under .035 and that its drift is this quantity; if either fails, the threshold is 0.04, RL-151 §1.3's own top cell.
decisions.action: print 'within' or 'to the research lead'; the exp form prints beside it

decisions.statistic: the maximum over counted days of the leave-one-day-out hot-stretch relative error (GPU rail)
decisions.rule: At or under the threshold: the interim half passes. Fewer than three counted days: not_evaluable, which is no. The qualification look supplies the other half. Its stated power and what no may not be read as are fit.stated_limits qualified_pass_rate and qualified_yes_meaning (RL-166b §2.1); the line itself is unchanged.
decisions.action: print passes, fails or not_evaluable; S_w and K_w stay print-only either way

decisions.statistic: hp-01 included legs from stage 1's inclusion table
decisions.rule: Fewer than 9 of 12: stage 1 goes to the research lead before stage 2, who rules on a second High Power block.
decisions.action: report; freeze 2 does not wait for hp-01

decisions.rule: Fewer than 45 development legs included; fewer than 4 calendar days (RL-166b B-7); a prompt-size cell with fewer than 10 included legs; more than 10 % of legs without a valid start reading; or hp-01 below 9: stage 1 goes to the research lead before stage 2. Otherwise stage 2 runs on the lead's record.
decisions.action: print each tripwire's count and whether it fired

decisions.statistic: legs on which analyse_leg raised, per cell
decisions.rule: More than two in a cell: that cell prints not_run and comes to the research lead.
No extension rule is written. RL-151 §2.2 already refused the legs an extension would buy; any extension beyond the cap needs a ruling.
decisions.action: print 'none written; any extension needs a ruling'

decisions.statistic: stage 1's count of legs that start in state with an observed onset under 116.0 s from the turn start (P-4)
decisions.rule: If the onset model is not_estimable and the count is above zero, the 116 s count-only cut does not stand by default: stage 1 comes to the research lead before stage 2.
decisions.action: print the count by G0 role and to_research_lead

declared_prints: the length-only bias at 1.10 and 1.30 in score SD, each with its 90 % interval against +/-0.10
the type-M residual as not_run (RL-165 §8.1 took type M out)
fewer than 3 days among the pairs prints not_evaluable for the +/-0.10 word; at 3 days the simulation puts a true bias of 0.01 inside +/-0.10 in 0.84 of runs, and lm-qual-01 states that (RL-166b §4)
the ratios 1.10, 1.30 and 1.374 name ratios of decode tokens; the ratio of load seconds prints by cell (RL-166b §4)
later_looks.scorer: fit_interim.py's predict path at the hash this manifest pins

the fit code's paths and hashes (fit.code)
the model family and predictor lists as RL-166 fixes them (fit.heat_term, fit.onset, fit.rates)
the inclusion rules and the code that judges rules 3 and 4
the step 3 code and its adapter (fit.step3)
freeze1.ledger_pointer: LOOKS.json records the manifest and roster commitments, the execution host and roots, any stage-1 clearing rulings, and the public report and coefficient hashes or the fixed failure type.

freeze2.artifact: SHA-256 of the exact RESTRICTED/coefficients.json bytes. PUBLIC.json on main establishes freeze 2 on twin_agrees = yes. With no or not_evaluable, the result is recorded and the research lead must rule before qualification arms or scoring uses the fit.
contents: the base and heat parameters per channel, with the leg-clustered covariance (S_w's SD_j)
the holdout RMS relative error (S_w's SD_j)
the start-reading medians and calibrated ranges (heat_extrapolated)
the onset model's coefficients, its error and the count-only cut, or not_estimable
the hashes of this manifest, the code that ran, stage 1's output and the private fit; the numpy version
the active readings (RL-166b B-2) and each fold's coefficient vector (P-1), which the SD_j rule reads
each held-out day's onset coefficients and scatter for the reference-turn day-jackknife, or null when delta is absent
used_by: the count-only cut's onset model (RL-149 §4 item 1)
lm-hp-01, which takes freeze 2's files by hash (RL-167 §3)

deferred_rules.rule: No single kappa's sign or size is read. Freeze 2 reports H with its interval for three reference turns, computed from the coefficient file. No energy is read for it.

SD_j's covariance term, for each reference turn, is the larger of the leg-clustered standard error and the day-jackknife value from P-1's fold coefficients: sqrt((D - 1)/D * sum over held-out days d of (H(-d) - their mean)^2). Fixed now so that it is not chosen after the output is seen.
A turn whose start readings lie further from the campaign's centre, by joint distance, than any campaign leg is flagged beside heat_extrapolated. Stage 1's committed readings are enough; no code now.
A turn with more than 10 expected hot seconds in its prefill, by RL-166b B-1's formula, is flagged.

custody.custody_copy: One verified custody copy of the roster's spans by the existing offload tooling, made while the MBP is unarmed; the look runs on that copy, never on the MBP's measurement root. The copy lives under the one root this manifest registers (root): each span at <root>/<span id>, and the look's own files at fixed names in <root>/lm-interim-01. Campaign stages take no path. Under RL-217 E.1 the rules-3/4 rehearsal creates a private directory outside the repository and every registered root. Stage-1 rehearsal reads the verdict and writes its own outputs there.
custody.host: Under RL-217 E.1 the draft LOOKS.json row registers the campaign host and both rehearsal commands check its host-id token. Under RL-184 the lead records the admitted commit's token in the stage1_committed row on main. Stage 2 recomputes it before reservation. A host change requires a new ledger row and confirmation that the first host has no reservation.
no_import_by: every frozen path of every leg kit
custody.disclosure: No number computed from energy is public before the data release. The public outputs are at most sixteen words, counts that hold no energy, and hashes. The look manifest's pin list carries the sha256 of each span's operational journal, which contains one measured idle-power mean; no value from it was read before the reservation. No Check item of 14 to 18 November printed its span's inventory digest in full. Each inventory is a sums file written at the span's close, fixed by the record of that close that RL-217 A names.
custody.pre_run_check: Review planted-truth synthetic bundles and run the energy-blind stage 1. The separately pinned twin runs inside the look after coefficients are final. It compares both channels' coefficients to 1e-8 relative, the censored fit to 1e-6, and verdict words, trace_coverage and soak_retries for equality. The ledger_gate is excluded.
custody.pin_check: Stage 1 and stage 2 verify the repository pins, stage-1 roster and verdict commitments, and the committed LOOKS.json row. Under RL-217 E.1 the stock rules-3/4 producer verifies the registered spans against the committed pins. Campaign stage 1 checks the stock receipt against the committed row, verdict bytes and input names and hashes. Every stage 1 that is not a draft run, campaign or rehearsal, derives its admission again at the end of preflight and immediately before its writes and refuses any change: the ledger gate and the committed row, then the stock receipt for a campaign run, or the registered host and the destination fence for a rehearsal. Stage 2 checks its host, both registered roots, the hold rulings, prior execution history and the twin pins before reserving RESTRICTED/ by exclusive mkdir. Stage 2 redirects stdout and stderr into RESTRICTED/ before opening a response file. An interrupted reservation spends the id and is recorded as interrupted with error_type none_recorded (RL-183). The parent captures both streams from the pinned isolated twin and adjudicates the stdout frame after writing the coefficient file (RL-181). A delivered RL-180 failure notice is recorded as failed with its closed type.

inputs.rule: The roster is a closed set, so stage 1 admits by content address. This list, the manifest's own and its only copy, pins by sha256 and size every file of every roster span; every reader reads it from here. A span's pins are the lines of its offload manifest in their order, so they rebuild that manifest's sha256, which the span's public RUN_STATE Check item names (after the span's own name, under an explicit "Offload manifest" identification, in full hex equal to the pin: an abbreviation, a pending digest, another label or any mismatch holds the span); no pin is hashed from today's copy. A separate hash-only verifier process runs first, before a stage parses anything and before the reservation: it reads every pinned file as opaque bytes and writes pass or fail with the pinned and observed digests. Each stage then reads the operational files it parses once, hashes them and parses those bytes, and refuses a missing, unpinned or symlinked file by name. Stage 1 never hashes an energy stream. Stage 2 re-checks a stream's pin immediately before decoding it, and the twin's wrapper checks every pin before the reviewed child runs byte-identical. The grammar validator still runs on the admitted bytes. A span whose Check item does not identify its offload manifest in full hex, every character matching and no manifest digest printed for the span contradicting it, is HELD: it keeps the manifest from being final and stays on the roster. Its check_item may be corrected only to an item that does (check_corrected_from keeps the item the pin table cited); a close-time outer.sha256 is cited as a second record only.
